project.name: assimp
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/assimp` is on commit `182418e8187ecf3d99b6c6c82836ab6fca14d87f`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below are resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `FileSystemFilter::Cleanup()` logic shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42495802 (assimp): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target assimp_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42495802
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json, reproduction_report.json, sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, patch.diff, trace_feedback.json, staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/assimp`, and staged `poc` bytes
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is a malformed LightWave `LWMO` text file with SHA-256 `3357a061e7e076e608f9a4b3feab565fb682434722bfcabac377998949e90b9d`. Its second top-level token begins with byte `0xff`, so `LWSImporter::InternReadFile()` computes `version = strtoul10((*it).tokens[0].c_str()) == 0` and later treats `LoadObject` records as legacy `version < 4` entries. The staged `poc` contains multiple reachable `LoadObject` filename tokens that still end with `:`, including repeated `fS:` entries and one `&fS:` entry. When `LWS::Element::Parse()` materializes such a `LoadObject` record, `InternReadFile()` binds `c` to that terminal-colon string, skips the `version >= 4` explicit-ID parsing that would otherwise advance `c`, and calls `FindLWOFile(c)`. These witness values do not match `FindLWOFile()`'s drive-letter repair pattern, so the same terminal-colon path is probed through `io->Exists(tmp)`. `FileSystemFilter::Exists()` copies that path into stack-local `tmp`, takes the auxiliary-file branch, runs `BuildPath(tmp)` (which for these slash-free witness values can only leave the string unchanged or prefix `./`, but preserves the attacker-controlled trailing `:` in either case), and then calls `Cleanup(tmp)`. Inside `Cleanup()`, the loop reaches the final `:` of that terminal-colon path and executes `strncmp(&*it, "://", 3)` without checking that three bytes remain. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 1-byte stack-buffer-overflow read with top frames `strncmp -> Assimp::FileSystemFilter::Cleanup -> Assimp::FileSystemFilter::Exists -> Assimp::LWSImporter::FindLWOFile`. The saved artifacts do not distinguish which terminal-colon `LoadObject` candidate reached the crashing call, and the staged patch fixes the missing obligation by computing `remaining` and guarding both `strncmp` probes before they are evaluated.

source.description: Source. `Parse()` copies the second top-level line's first token from attacker-controlled LWMO text into `tokens[0]`; on this witness that token starts with byte `0xff`, so the later numeric conversion yields `version == 0` and selects legacy `LoadObject` path handling.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` starts with bytes `4c 57 4d 4f 0a ff 30`; after `LWMO\n`, `Parse()` stores the next line's first token as a string beginning with byte `0xff` followed by ASCII `0`.
source.note: This is the earliest project statement that creates vulnerability-relevant control state for the later `LoadObject` filename binding.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `Cleanup()` probes for `://` with `strncmp(&*it, ..., 3)` at each iterator position but never checks that at least 3 characters remain. On the witnessed terminal-colon path copied into `tmp`, the final iterator position leaves too few bytes for that probe.
root_cause.note: The staged patch computes `remaining` inside this loop and requires `remaining >= 3` before the `strncmp` call.

sink.description: Project-level crash site. When `it` points at the terminal `:` of the short stack path built from attacker input, this call asks `strncmp` to read three bytes from a one-character suffix. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting stack-buffer-overflow read from `tmp` in `FileSystemFilter::Exists()`.
sink.note: The saved ASan stack is `strncmp -> Assimp::FileSystemFilter::Cleanup -> Assimp::FileSystemFilter::Exists -> Assimp::IOSystem::Exists -> Assimp::LWSImporter::FindLWOFile`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled filename bytes that drive the bug are bound here from a parsed `LoadObject` record whose filename token ends with `:`. Because `version` was already set to 0 on the witness, the later explicit-ID arm does not advance `c`, so `FindLWOFile()` sees that same terminal-colon token.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Static inspection of the staged `poc` shows repeated `LoadObject\tfS:` records at offsets 724, 1337, 2103, 3521, 4174, 4548, 4922, 5296, 5670, and 6044, plus one `LoadObject\t&fS:` record at offset 1773. The saved trace also logs both `Invalid path: fS:` and `Invalid path: &fS:` before the crash. When the loop reaches any such terminal-colon element, `(*it).tokens[1]` yields a filename string that still ends with `:`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The crash depends on this bound string retaining the attacker-controlled trailing `:` through the later lookup and normalization helpers.

parser_admitted.description: The saved run logs show the importer accepted the in-memory witness as LightWave scene data and advanced into parsed version/object processing before the crash.
parser_admitted.note: The saved trace prints `Found a matching importer for this file format: LightWave Scene Importer.` and then `LWS file format version is ...` before the ASan stack, proving `root.Parse(dummy)` completed and `InternReadFile()` was iterating parsed elements.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not instrument the ARVO workspace. The chain is grounded only in staged source, patch.diff, trace_feedback.json, saved ASan traces, reproduction_report.json, and static inspection of `poc` bytes.

The staged `poc` contains multiple `LoadObject` filename tokens that end with `:`, including repeated `fS:` and one `&fS:`. Saved artifacts do not identify which terminal-colon candidate reached the final crashing `FindLWOFile()`/`Exists()`/`Cleanup()` path, so this GT attributes the sink flow only to a reached terminal-colon `LoadObject` token on the witnessed `version < 4` path.

The saved traces do not expose whether `BuildPath(tmp)` left the lookup string unchanged or prefixed `./` before `Cleanup()`. The GT therefore claims only the source-grounded invariant that `BuildPath()` preserves the attacker-controlled trailing `:` for these slash-free witness values.

Stage 02 does not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` adds explicit remaining-length guards before the crashing `strncmp` probes.

coarse_trace.summary: The LWS parser stores a malformed version token beginning with `0xff`, and `InternReadFile()` converts it to numeric `version == 0`, selecting the legacy `LoadObject` path-handling branch.

A later `LoadObject` record whose filename token ends with `:` is parsed; when the loop reaches that element, `c` is bound to this value and the `version >= 4` explicit-ID parse is skipped, so the whole terminal-colon token is forwarded.
The witness's terminal-colon `LoadObject` candidates do not match `FindLWOFile()`'s drive-letter repair pattern and are probed through `io->Exists(tmp)`.

The filesystem filter copies the attacker path into stack `tmp`, takes the auxiliary-file branch, and runs `BuildPath(tmp)` before `Cleanup(tmp)`, preserving the trailing colon even if `./` is prefixed.
The cleanup loop reaches the terminal `:` of the terminal-colon path and calls `strncmp(&*it, "://", 3)` without a remaining-length guard, producing the saved stack-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the second top-level line of the staged LWMO text, `Parse()` stores a token beginning with byte `0xff` and trailing ASCII `0`.
Later in the same parse, when the parser reaches a `LoadObject` record whose filename field still ends with `:`, it materializes that terminal-colon value as `tokens[1]`.

depends_on.via: the same recursive Parse() continues across later LWMO records

fine_trace.note: When `InternReadFile()` advances to the second parsed root element, `strtoul10()` sees the step-1 token start with `0xff`, consumes no digits, and yields `version == 0`. Later object records therefore follow the `version < 4` branch.
On the relevant `LoadObject` element, `c` is initialized from step 2 so it points at the full terminal-colon filename token before any per-version rewriting.

Because step 3 made `version < 4`, the explicit-ID path is not taken. The `strtoul16(c, &c); SkipSpaces(&c);` pair that would otherwise consume an explicit object ID and advance `c` is skipped, so `c` still points to the whole terminal-colon filename token when file lookup begins.

FindLWOFile copies the caller's path into local `tmp`; its drive-letter repair at lines 467-468 does not run for the witness's terminal-colon candidates because they are not of the form `<letter>:` followed by a missing separator, so this `io->Exists(tmp)` probe uses the same terminal-colon string.

The probed filename is copied into stack-local `std::string tmp`. On the witness this local string starts from attacker bytes that still end with `:`, and ASan reports the overflowing object as `tmp` in this frame.
This lookup is for an auxiliary object file, not the top-level memory-backed scene name `$$$___magic___$$$.`, so `tmp != mSrc_file` is true and the path-normalization helpers execute.

With `mBase == "./"` from the filter constructor and an input containing no slash or backslash, `BuildPath()` can only leave `tmp` unchanged or prefix `./` before it if a base-relative candidate exists; it cannot remove or move the attacker-controlled terminal `:`.
No leading-space trim applies to the terminal-colon path from step 9. `Cleanup()` advances `it` to its final `:`, and at that iterator position fewer than 3 characters remain before `in.end()`.

Root cause and sink. `Cleanup()` calls `strncmp` on `&*it` without first checking that 3 bytes remain. When step 10 has `it` on the final `:` of the terminal-colon path from step 9, the interceptor reads past stack `tmp`, matching the saved 1-byte ASan stack-buffer-overflow at this line.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the overflowing object as local stack `tmp` in this frame, occupying `[32, 56)`.

crash_stack.function: Assimp::Importer::ReadFileFromMemory(void const*, unsigned long, unsigned int, char const*)

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Runtime frame 0 is the `strncmp` interceptor; runtime frame 1 and the dedup token both identify `Assimp::FileSystemFilter::Cleanup` at the sink line.

poc.trigger: Import the staged in-memory `LWMO` text until the malformed second-line version token makes `version == 0`, a reachable `LoadObject` record whose filename token still ends with `:` binds `c` under the `version < 4` branch, and `FileSystemFilter::Cleanup()` evaluates the `://` check on that terminal colon.

format.name: LWMO text scene
format.contract: Exact staged witness only: the text file from `poc` starts with `LWMO`, its second top-level token begins with byte `0xff` so `strtoul10()` yields 0, and it contains multiple `LoadObject` filename tokens that still end with `:`, including repeated `fS:` records and one `&fS:` record. Saved artifacts establish only that one such terminal-colon filename reached `FindLWOFile()`/`Exists()`/`Cleanup()` on the witnessed `version < 4` path; they do not distinguish which candidate did.
